technical_facts: Modified QuakeEd to retrieve programs from id1_
Added color support to QuakeEd entities
Removed /lquake and migrated QuakeEd caches to /qcache
Implemented a mechanism to wait for a second message acknowledgment before accepting datagrams
Added water friction and swimming bubble sound effects
Modified QuakeEd start position to use playerstart
Combined damage messages for super shotgun blasts
personality_patterns: Highly task-oriented, focusing on a granular list of bug fixes and feature additions
Preference for concise, shorthand notation in tracking progress
Systematic approach to iterating on game mechanics (physics, audio, visuals)

gnosis_principles.description: Breaking down complex system development into small, verifiable tasks (e.g., 'swimming bubble noise', 'drowning damage') to ensure steady progress.
Consolidating and relocating cache directories (e.g., moving QuakeEd caches to /qcache) to streamline system organization.

heritage_patterns: The use of a '.plan' file for public, transparent development logging
Fast-paced, iterative bug-fixing cycles typical of early id Software development
Low-level optimization of network datagram handling for multiplayer stability

dpo_pairs.prompt: What changes did Carmack make to QuakeEd in the March 1996 plan?
dpo_pairs.chosen: Carmack updated QuakeEd to retrieve programs from id1_, added colors to entities, and moved caches from /lquake to /qcache.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He made some general improvements to the editor and changed how files were stored.

dpo_pairs.prompt: How did Carmack handle network datagrams in this update?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He implemented a rule to not take datagrams until the second message is acknowledged.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He optimized the network code to make the game run faster.
